text: Captain George John Sandys (/ˈsændz/; 23 September 1875 – 3 September 1937) was a British diplomat and Conservative politician. He was the son of James Sandys of Slade House, Stroud, Gloucestershire, and was educated at Clifton College and Pembroke College, Oxford.[1] He was commissioned as a second lieutenant and served with the Glamorgan Yeomanry during the Second Boer War from 1899, then transferred to the regular army when he became a second lieutenant in the 5th Dragoon Guards on 15 August 1900, receiving a promotion to lieutenant on 28 August 1901 while still in South Africa.[2] After the war ended, he transferred to the 2nd Life Guards in November 1902,[3] leaving the army in 1905. He rejoined to serve in the British Expeditionary Force during the First World War and was wounded at Ypres.[4] Sandys was a Member of Parliament for Wells from 1910 to 1918. He later joined the diplomatic service, serving as an Honorary Attaché in the British Legation in Bern (1921–22) and Paris (1922–25).[1] He married Mildred Helen, née Cameron, daughter of Duncan Cameron of Canterbury, New Zealand, in 1905.[5] They had one child, a son named Duncan Sandys.[4] Duncan became a member of parliament and cabinet minister, and Duncan's daughter Laura Sandys, also a Conservative politician, was elected to represent South Thanet in 2010.[6] Sandys divorced Mildred in January 1921.[5][7] He died in Antibes, France on 3 September 1937.[8]
